decision: Where2comm is frozen as THE external baseline. ML-Cooper and SmartCooper are cited as related work and NOT reimplemented. P0-7 is registered UNMET (V2-R32 A-1).
P0_7: UNMET -- no candidate was chosen to fill the slot; see docs/tier_c_external_baseline_selection.md

negative_existence_claim.method: web search per candidate with github / code release / channel-aware, plus two collaborative-perception paper-digest repositories
negative_existence_claim.conclusion: NO official runnable repository or weights found WITHIN THE PRE-REGISTERED SCOPE
negative_existence_claim.not_claimed: that no such release exists anywhere (A-2)

smartcooper_principled_misalignment.separate_from: the no-public-code finding -- this is a DISTINCT reason and is recorded on its own (A-3)
smartcooper_principled_misalignment.reason: SmartCooper contribution IS a learnable CSI-conditioned compression ratio, so its payload is an output of its own encoder. Forcing it onto the fixed w=8 / N_cw chain deletes the mechanism under comparison; leaving it free makes the two arms not budget-matched.

mlcooper_exclusion.reason: reimplementing an unreleased method and then comparing against it carries no information -- consistent with the SComCP lesson, where a self-built scaffold that failed to reproduce demonstrated something about the scaffold, not about the method (A-4)

frozen_configuration.code: baselines/where2comm_v2/ in THIS repository (run_inference.py, score_arm.py, transport_replay.py, intersection_gt_track.py, paired_bootstrap.py)

upstream_commit.implementation: opencood/models/fuse_modules/where2comm_fuse.py -- OpenCOOD OWN implementation of Where2comm, NOT a port of MediaBrain-SJTU/where2comm
upstream_commit.how_established: the training tree /mnt/h/wsl_backup/OpenCOOD_20260601_1326 is itself a git checkout; git rev-parse HEAD returns the same base commit as the sibling

checkpoint.evidence: 50 net_epochN.pth files and a TensorBoard events.out.tfevents.* in the directory -- the signature of a training run, not a download. Trained 2026-05-22.
checkpoint.loaded_epoch: 50 (load_saved_model takes the highest epoch; no bestval/latest file present)
checkpoint.no_retraining_at_N1: the arm does NOT retrain at N=1; CATOSG_MAX_COLLAB is an inference-time hook

frozen_configuration.collaborator_rule: CATOSG_MAX_COLLAB=1, inference-time hook; NO retraining (the arm refuses to retrain at N=1, which would treat it differently from every other arm)
frozen_configuration.control_variable: the communication THRESHOLD, not a sparsity s -- the rate is an OUTPUT, measured per frame as mask.sum()/(L*H*W)
frozen_configuration.payload: counterfactual under the pre-registered sparse convention; the realised mean rate is what the budget match uses
frozen_configuration.WORDING_CORRECTION: The R51 change log says the arm runs "on public pretrained checkpoints, with no retraining". That sentence is about not retraining AT N=1, and it is true in that sense -- but read plainly it suggests OFFICIAL weights, and the weights are locally trained. Corrected here so the freeze record cannot be read the wrong way.

wording_rules_unchanged: R60-2 stands: Where2comm is an external feature-content / communication-efficient baseline, NOT a channel-aware granularity selector isomorphic to CA-TOSG. Adjudication verbs remain forbidden everywhere, with no exemption (B-6).

DETERMINISTIC_REGENERATION_REQUIRED.status: TODO at WP12 -- these numbers are PROVISIONAL until then
DETERMINISTIC_REGENERATION_REQUIRED.why: the existing Where2comm products were generated around R60-2, i.e. under the OLD non-deterministic shuffle_points() pipeline that V2-R16 found and fixed. V2-R16 E-3 requires any v1-derived baseline still used for a v2 comparison to be regenerated under the deterministic pipeline. Where2comm is now exactly such a baseline.
DETERMINISTIC_REGENERATION_REQUIRED.RULE: A freeze check may NEVER pass on the ground that the files already exist. Existence is not provenance, and a hash matching a non-deterministic product only proves the bytes have not moved since (C-4).
